name: Alanylglutamine
description: A glutamine-containing dipeptide used as a nutrient source in some cell-culture media.

name: Angiotensin II
description: An octapeptide studied in receptor signaling and cardiovascular physiology.

name: Anserine
description: A methylated relative of carnosine found in skeletal muscle.

name: Aspartame
description: A dipeptide methyl ester commonly discussed in food chemistry.

name: Carnosine
description: A β-alanine-containing dipeptide used to study buffering in muscle.

name: Cysteinylglycine
description: A thiol-containing dipeptide formed during glutathione breakdown.

name: Gancidin W
description: A cyclic dipeptide with a 2,5-diketopiperazine ring.

name: GHK
description: The free tripeptide ligand used in copper-binding studies. This record shows the peptide before metal coordination.

name: Glutathione
description: A redox tripeptide. Glutamate is linked through its side-chain carboxyl group.

name: Glutathione disulfide
description: Two glutathione molecules joined by a cysteine disulfide bond.

name: Glycylglycine
description: The simplest dipeptide. Also used as a buffer in biochemical experiments.

name: Glycylproline
description: A dipeptide that illustrates the cyclic proline residue and its substituted peptide nitrogen.

name: Met-enkephalin
description: An opioid pentapeptide. The NMR model was measured in a lipid bicelle preparation.

name: Muramyl dipeptide
description: A peptidoglycan fragment used in research on innate immune recognition.

name: Ophthalmic acid
description: A glutathione analogue with α-aminobutyrate in place of cysteine.

name: Oxytocin
description: A nonapeptide with an amidated C-terminus and a Cys¹–Cys⁶ disulfide bridge.

name: Protirelin
description: An amidated tripeptide with a pyroglutamyl N-terminus.

name: Valyltyrosine
description: A dipeptide with an aromatic tyrosine side chain.
